task_instance: Scaffold a new Codex plugin named 'My Cool Plugin' in a sample repo root: create <repo>/plugins/my-cool-plugin/.codex-plugin/plugin.json (full manifest schema with TODO placeholders), optional companion folders/files (skills/, hooks/, scripts/, assets/, .mcp.json, .app.json), and register it in <repo>/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json with policy.installation, policy.authentication, and category fields, matching the exact shapes documented in SKILL.md.
blocker_detail: Note: the skill's own referenced scaffold script (scripts/create_basic_plugin.py under .agents/skills/plugin-creator/) was not present in the provided skill source directory (only SKILL.md and LICENSE existed). This did not block the task: the script's exact behavior (name normalization rules, plugin.json schema, marketplace.json schema/defaults) is fully specified in SKILL.md, so a reimplementation was written from that spec and used to produce and verify the deliverable.
evidence: Work dir: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-skill-achievability-compiler/a1321181-416f-5422-8c3b-9ffc8650b51c/scratchpad/exec_ext/openai__skills__plugin-creator. Wrote create_basic_plugin.py (reimplementing the documented scaffold behavior) and ran it against a sample repo (sample_repo/): `python3 ../create_basic_plugin.py "My Cool Plugin" --path plugins --with-skills --with-hooks --with-scripts --with-assets --with-mcp --with-apps --with-marketplace --marketplace-path .agents/plugins/marketplace.json`. Verified output tree contains plugins/my-cool-plugin/.codex-plugin/plugin.json, .mcp.json, .app.json, and skills/hooks/scripts/assets folders. Confirmed name normalization 'My Cool Plugin' -> 'my-cool-plugin' (folder name and plugin.json 'name' match). plugin.json contains full manifest shape (name, version, description, author, license, interface{displayName, icon, category}) with '[TODO: ...]' placeholders as required. marketplace.json created fresh with required top-level shape (name, interface.displayName placeholders, plugins[]) and one entry containing name, source.source='local', source.path='./plugins/my-cool-plugin', policy.installation='AVAILABLE', policy.authentication='ON_INSTALL', category='Productivity' -- matching the exact sample in SKILL.md. Verified both plugin.json and marketplace.json parse as valid JSON via `python3 -c "import json; json.load(open(...))"`. Also unit-tested normalize_name() against SKILL.md's stated rules ('My Plugin'->'my-plugin', 'My--Plugin'->'my-plugin', underscore/punctuation collapsing) -- all passed. Tested --force semantics: re-running without --force on an existing plugin path correctly raised FileExistsError; re-running with --force succeeded and left both JSON files valid.
